These are three separate companies, but are together called the [[:en:Hitotsubashi Group|Hitotsubashi Group]],{{cite news|title=Global Publishing Leaders 2015: Shogakukan|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/67308-global-publishing-leaders-2015-shogakukan.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=26 Jun 2015}} one of the largest publishing groups in Japan and the world. Shogakukan is headquartered in the Shogakukan Building in [[:en:Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|Hitotsubashi]], part of [[:en:Kanda, Tokyo|Kanda]], [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda, Tokyo]], near the [[:en:Jimbocho|Jimbocho]] book district. The corporation also has the other two companies located in the same [[:en:23 special wards|ward]]. ==International operations== ===In the United States=== Shogakukan, along with [[:en:Shueisha|Shueisha]], owns [[:en:Viz Media|Viz Media]],{{cite news|last1=Alverson|first1=Brigid|title=Hachette and Kadokawa Partner on Manga and Graphic Novels|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/70380-hachette-and-kadokawa-partner-on-manga-and-graphic-novels.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=13 May 2016}} which publishes manga from both companies in the [[:en:United States|United States]]. Shogakukan's licensing arm in North America was '''ShoPro Entertainment'''; it was merged into Viz Media in 2005.{{cite news|title=ShoPro Entertainment Inc. and VIZ, LLC to Merge|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2005-01-25/shopro-entertainment-inc-and-viz-llc-to-merge|access-date=23 April 2018|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Jan 2005}} Shogakukan's production arm is [[:en:Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions]] (previously Shogakukan Productions Co., Ltd.) In March 2010 it was announced that Shogakukan would partner with the American comics publisher [[:en:Fantagraphics|Fantagraphics]] to issue a line of manga to be edited by [[:en:Rachel Thorn|Rachel Thorn]].{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100738/http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|archive-date=September 7, 2015|url=http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|title=Journalista reputation-destroying extra: Four years' work|last=Deppey|first=Dirk|date=March 8, 2010|work=Journalista!|publisher=The Comics Journal|access-date=2015-11-16}} ===In Europe=== In [[:en:Europe|Europe]], manga from Shōgakukan and [[:en:Shūeisha|Shūeisha]] are published by local publishers such as [[:en:Pika Édition|Pika Édition]], [[:en:Ki-oon|Ki-oon]], [[:en:Kana (publisher)|Kana]] and [[:en:Kazé|Kazé]] for the French market, and Kazé, [[:en:Carlsen Verlag|Carlsen]], [[Egmont Group#Egmont Publishing|Egmont]] and [[:en:Tokyopop|Tokyopop]] for the German market. Shogakukan, Shueisha and ShoPro have established a joint venture named [[:en:Viz Media Europe|Viz Media Europe]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |title=Vizmedia Europe rachète le groupe Kazé |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181304/http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |url-status=dead }} Viz Media Europe bought in 2009 the French Kazé Group whose activities are mainly publishing manga and home video for the French and German market.{{Cite web |url=http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |title=Organisation du groupe Vizmedia Europe |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627071327/http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |url-status=dead }} ===In Southeast Asia=== The company has a wholly-owned subsidiary, [[:en:Shogakukan Asia|Shogakukan Asia]], with headquarter in [[:en:Singapore|Singapore]]. Besides producing popular titles in English such as ''[[:en:Case Closed|Detective Conan]]'', ''[[:en:Pokémon|Pokémon]]'' and ''[[:en:Future Card Buddyfight|Future Card Buddyfight]]'', the company also partners with local creators such as [[:en:Johnny Lau|Johnny Lau]] to publish comic series for distribution in Southeast Asia."[https://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/news-and-events/news/singapore-business-news/Industry/education-through-entertainment.html Education through entertainment]" (). [[:en:Singapore Economic Development Board|Singapore Economic Development Board]]. January 15, 2014. Retrieved on June 2, 2015. ==New Manga Awards== Shogakukan has awards for amateur [[:en:Mangaka|manga artists]] who want to become professional. It allows people to either send in their [[:en:Manga|Manga]] by mail or bring it in to an [[:en:Editor|Editor]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Genghis Khan controversy== {{weight|date=May 2023}} On February 15, 2018, ''[[:en:CoroCoro Comic|CoroCoro Comic]]'' ( "''Gekkan Corocoro Comic''"), a children's magazine published by Shogakukan, had in its March issue a cartoon making fun of [[:en:Genghis Khan|Genghis Khan]], founder of the [[:en:Toluid Civil War|Mongol Empire]]. The comic showed a mischievous boy doodling juvenile things on pictures of famous people, such as a dog's face on a picture of [[:en:Albert Einstein|Albert Einstein]]. Genghis Khan was depicted with a crude rendering of male genitalia on his forehead.{{cite news|title=Mongolians irate over manga showing penis on Genghis Khan|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=28 February 2018|archive-date=August 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802191717/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Coro Coro Comics Apologizes for Manga's Depiction of Genghis Khan|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2018-02-25/coro-coro-comics-apologizes-for-manga-depiction-of-genghis-khan/.128187|access-date=13 June 2020|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Feb 2018}} After some backlash, Shogakukan initially offered an apology addressed to the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo on February 23, but that failed to mollify Mongolian expats in Japan, who regard Genghis Khan as a national hero. On February 26, Mongolians and citizens of [[:en:China Airlines|China]]'s [[:en:Inner Mongolia|Inner Mongolia]] [[:en:Autonomous regions of China|autonomous region]] resident in Japan sent a formal letter of protest to Shogakukan, while some 90 demonstrators protested in front of company headquarters. Major bookselling chains [[:en:Kinokuniya|Kinokuniya]], Miraiya and Kumazawa pulled the publication off shelves after the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo filed an official complaint with the [[:en:Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]].{{cite web|title=Genghis Khan-insulting manga pulled from major book stores amid further Mongolian protests|url=https://soranews24.com/2018/03/01/genghis-khan-insulting-manga-pulled-from-major-book-stores-amid-further-mongolian-protests/|website=SoraNews24|date=March 2018|publisher=Socio Corporation|access-date=13 June 2020}} In March 2018, Shogakukan issued another public apology, announced a national recall of the magazine and offered a refund to magazine patrons.{{cite news|title=Publisher Shogakukan withdraws and apologizes for comic that mocks Genghis Khan|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/03/06/national/japanese-publisher-withdraws-kids-comic-illustration-mocks-mongolian-hero-genghis-khan/|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=Kyodo|publisher=The Japan Times|date=6 March 2018}} CoroCoro Comic's website also published an apology by Asumi Yoshino, author of the serialized manga ''Yarisugi!!! Itazura-kun'' which contained the controversial image.{{cite news|last1=Shiohara|first1=Ken|title=Publisher recalls manga magazine that infuriated Mongolians|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=7 March 2018|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630024803/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|url-status=dead}} ==List of magazines published== ===Manga magazines=== ====Male oriented manga magazines==== ;Children's manga magazines *''[[:en:CoroCoro Comic|CoroCoro Comic]]'' (since 1977) *''Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic'' (since 1981) *''CoroCoro Ichiban!'' These are three separate companies, but are together called the [[:en:Hitotsubashi Group|Hitotsubashi Group]],{{cite news|title=Global Publishing Leaders 2015: Shogakukan|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/67308-global-publishing-leaders-2015-shogakukan.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=26 Jun 2015}} one of the largest publishing groups in Japan and the world. Shogakukan is headquartered in the Shogakukan Building in [[:en:Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|Hitotsubashi]], part of [[:en:Kanda, Tokyo|Kanda]], [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda, Tokyo]], near the [[:en:Jimbocho|Jimbocho]] book district. The corporation also has the other two companies located in the same [[:en:23 special wards|ward]]. ==International operations== ===In the United States=== Shogakukan, along with [[:en:Shueisha|Shueisha]], owns [[:en:Viz Media|Viz Media]],{{cite news|last1=Alverson|first1=Brigid|title=Hachette and Kadokawa Partner on Manga and Graphic Novels|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/70380-hachette-and-kadokawa-partner-on-manga-and-graphic-novels.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=13 May 2016}} which publishes manga from both companies in the [[:en:United States|United States]]. Shogakukan's licensing arm in North America was '''ShoPro Entertainment'''; it was merged into Viz Media in 2005.{{cite news|title=ShoPro Entertainment Inc. and VIZ, LLC to Merge|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2005-01-25/shopro-entertainment-inc-and-viz-llc-to-merge|access-date=23 April 2018|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Jan 2005}} Shogakukan's production arm is [[:en:Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions]] (previously Shogakukan Productions Co., Ltd.) In March 2010 it was announced that Shogakukan would partner with the American comics publisher [[:en:Fantagraphics|Fantagraphics]] to issue a line of manga to be edited by [[:en:Rachel Thorn|Rachel Thorn]].{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100738/http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|archive-date=September 7, 2015|url=http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|title=Journalista reputation-destroying extra: Four years' work|last=Deppey|first=Dirk|date=March 8, 2010|work=Journalista!|publisher=The Comics Journal|access-date=2015-11-16}} ===In Europe=== In [[:en:Europe|Europe]], manga from Shōgakukan and [[:en:Shūeisha|Shūeisha]] are published by local publishers such as [[:en:Pika Édition|Pika Édition]], [[:en:Ki-oon|Ki-oon]], [[:en:Kana (publisher)|Kana]] and [[:en:Kazé|Kazé]] for the French market, and Kazé, [[:en:Carlsen Verlag|Carlsen]], [[Egmont Group#Egmont Publishing|Egmont]] and [[:en:Tokyopop|Tokyopop]] for the German market. Shogakukan, Shueisha and ShoPro have established a joint venture named [[:en:Viz Media Europe|Viz Media Europe]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |title=Vizmedia Europe rachète le groupe Kazé |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181304/http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |url-status=dead }} Viz Media Europe bought in 2009 the French Kazé Group whose activities are mainly publishing manga and home video for the French and German market.{{Cite web |url=http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |title=Organisation du groupe Vizmedia Europe |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627071327/http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |url-status=dead }} ===In Southeast Asia=== The company has a wholly-owned subsidiary, [[:en:Shogakukan Asia|Shogakukan Asia]], with headquarter in [[:en:Singapore|Singapore]]. Besides producing popular titles in English such as ''[[:en:Case Closed|Detective Conan]]'', ''[[:en:Pokémon|Pokémon]]'' and ''[[:en:Future Card Buddyfight|Future Card Buddyfight]]'', the company also partners with local creators such as [[:en:Johnny Lau|Johnny Lau]] to publish comic series for distribution in Southeast Asia."[https://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/news-and-events/news/singapore-business-news/Industry/education-through-entertainment.html Education through entertainment]" (). [[:en:Singapore Economic Development Board|Singapore Economic Development Board]]. January 15, 2014. Retrieved on June 2, 2015. ==New Manga Awards== Shogakukan has awards for amateur [[:en:Mangaka|manga artists]] who want to become professional. It allows people to either send in their [[:en:Manga|Manga]] by mail or bring it in to an [[:en:Editor|Editor]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Genghis Khan controversy== {{weight|date=May 2023}} On February 15, 2018, ''[[:en:CoroCoro Comic|CoroCoro Comic]]'' ( "''Gekkan Corocoro Comic''"), a children's magazine published by Shogakukan, had in its March issue a cartoon making fun of [[:en:Genghis Khan|Genghis Khan]], founder of the [[:en:Toluid Civil War|Mongol Empire]]. The comic showed a mischievous boy doodling juvenile things on pictures of famous people, such as a dog's face on a picture of [[:en:Albert Einstein|Albert Einstein]]. Genghis Khan was depicted with a crude rendering of male genitalia on his forehead.{{cite news|title=Mongolians irate over manga showing penis on Genghis Khan|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=28 February 2018|archive-date=August 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802191717/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Coro Coro Comics Apologizes for Manga's Depiction of Genghis Khan|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2018-02-25/coro-coro-comics-apologizes-for-manga-depiction-of-genghis-khan/.128187|access-date=13 June 2020|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Feb 2018}} After some backlash, Shogakukan initially offered an apology addressed to the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo on February 23, but that failed to mollify Mongolian expats in Japan, who regard Genghis Khan as a national hero. On February 26, Mongolians and citizens of [[:en:China Airlines|China]]'s [[:en:Inner Mongolia|Inner Mongolia]] [[:en:Autonomous regions of China|autonomous region]] resident in Japan sent a formal letter of protest to Shogakukan, while some 90 demonstrators protested in front of company headquarters. Major bookselling chains [[:en:Kinokuniya|Kinokuniya]], Miraiya and Kumazawa pulled the publication off shelves after the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo filed an official complaint with the [[:en:Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]].{{cite web|title=Genghis Khan-insulting manga pulled from major book stores amid further Mongolian protests|url=https://soranews24.com/2018/03/01/genghis-khan-insulting-manga-pulled-from-major-book-stores-amid-further-mongolian-protests/|website=SoraNews24|date=March 2018|publisher=Socio Corporation|access-date=13 June 2020}} In March 2018, Shogakukan issued another public apology, announced a national recall of the magazine and offered a refund to magazine patrons.{{cite news|title=Publisher Shogakukan withdraws and apologizes for comic that mocks Genghis Khan|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/03/06/national/japanese-publisher-withdraws-kids-comic-illustration-mocks-mongolian-hero-genghis-khan/|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=Kyodo|publisher=The Japan Times|date=6 March 2018}} CoroCoro Comic's website also published an apology by Asumi Yoshino, author of the serialized manga ''Yarisugi!!! Itazura-kun'' which contained the controversial image.{{cite news|last1=Shiohara|first1=Ken|title=Publisher recalls manga magazine that infuriated Mongolians|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=7 March 2018|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630024803/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|url-status=dead}} ==List of magazines published== ===Manga magazines=== ====Male oriented manga magazines==== ;Children's manga magazines *''[[:en:CoroCoro Comic|CoroCoro Comic]]'' (since 1977) *''Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic'' (since 1981) *''CoroCoro Ichiban!'' (since 2005) ;''Shōnen'' manga magazines *''[[:en:Weekly Shōnen Sunday|Weekly Shōnen Sunday]]'' (since 1959) *''[[:en:Shōnen Sunday Super|Shōnen Sunday Super]]'' (since 1978) *''[[:en:Shōnen Big April 2018}} Shogakukan founded {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, which also founded {{ill|Hakusensha|en|Hakusensha|WD=Q1155260|lt=Hakusensha}}. These are three separate companies, but are together called the {{ill|Hitotsubashi Group|en|Hitotsubashi Group|WD=Q97352307|lt=Hitotsubashi Group}},{{cite news|title=Global Publishing Leaders 2015: Shogakukan|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/67308-global-publishing-leaders-2015-shogakukan.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=26 Jun 2015}} one of the largest publishing groups in Japan and the world. Shogakukan is headquartered in the Shogakukan Building in {{ill|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|en|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|WD=Q3347238|lt=Hitotsubashi}}, part of {{ill|Kanda, Tokyo|en|Kanda, Tokyo|WD=Q338861|lt=Kanda}}, {{ill|Chiyoda, Tokyo|en|Chiyoda, Tokyo|WD=Q214051|lt=Chiyoda, Tokyo}}, near the [[:en:Jimbocho|Jimbocho]] book district. The corporation also has the other two companies located in the same [[:en:23 special wards|ward]]. ==International operations== ===In the United States=== Shogakukan, along with {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, owns {{ill|Viz Media|en|Viz Media|WD=Q660288|lt=Viz Media}},{{cite news|last1=Alverson|first1=Brigid|title=Hachette and Kadokawa Partner on Manga and Graphic Novels|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/70380-hachette-and-kadokawa-partner-on-manga-and-graphic-novels.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=13 May 2016}} which publishes manga from both companies in the {{ill|United States|en|United States|WD=Q30|lt=United States}}. Shogakukan's licensing arm in North America was '''ShoPro Entertainment'''; it was merged into Viz Media in 2005.{{cite news|title=ShoPro Entertainment Inc. and VIZ, LLC to Merge|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2005-01-25/shopro-entertainment-inc-and-viz-llc-to-merge|access-date=23 April 2018|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Jan 2005}} Shogakukan's production arm is {{ill|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|en|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|WD=Q5356388|lt=Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions}} (previously Shogakukan Productions Co., Ltd.) In March 2010 it was announced that Shogakukan would partner with the American comics publisher {{ill|Fantagraphics|en|Fantagraphics|WD=Q1395850|lt=Fantagraphics}} to issue a line of manga to be edited by {{ill|Rachel Thorn|en|Rachel Thorn|WD=Q15500705|lt=Rachel Thorn}}.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100738/http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|archive-date=September 7, 2015|url=http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|title=Journalista reputation-destroying extra: Four years' work|last=Deppey|first=Dirk|date=March 8, 2010|work=Journalista!|publisher=The Comics Journal|access-date=2015-11-16}} ===In Europe=== In {{ill|Europe|en|Europe|WD=Q46|lt=Europe}}, manga from Shōgakukan and [[:en:Shūeisha|Shūeisha]] are published by local publishers such as {{ill|Pika Édition|en|Pika Édition|WD=Q3388349|lt=Pika Édition}}, {{ill|Ki-oon|en|Ki-oon|WD=Q3196283|lt=Ki-oon}}, {{ill|Kana (publisher)|en|Kana (publisher)|WD=Q2339813|lt=Kana}} and {{ill|Kazé|en|Kazé|WD=Q1582074|lt=Kazé}} for the French market, and Kazé, {{ill|Carlsen Verlag|en|Carlsen Verlag|WD=Q289299|lt=Carlsen}}, [[Egmont Group#Egmont Publishing|Egmont]] and {{ill|Tokyopop|en|Tokyopop|WD=Q315736|lt=Tokyopop}} for the German market. Shogakukan, Shueisha and ShoPro have established a joint venture named [[:en:Viz Media Europe|Viz Media Europe]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |title=Vizmedia Europe rachète le groupe Kazé |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181304/http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |url-status=dead }} Viz Media Europe bought in 2009 the French Kazé Group whose activities are mainly publishing manga and home video for the French and German market.{{Cite web |url=http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |title=Organisation du groupe Vizmedia Europe |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627071327/http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |url-status=dead }} ===In Southeast Asia=== The company has a wholly-owned subsidiary, {{ill|Shogakukan Asia|en|Shogakukan Asia|WD=Q20539280|lt=Shogakukan Asia}}, with headquarter in {{ill|Singapore|en|Singapore|WD=Q334|lt=Singapore}}. Besides producing popular titles in English such as ''{{ill|Case Closed|en|Case Closed|WD=Q3853685|lt=Detective Conan}}'', ''{{ill|Pokémon|en|Pokémon|WD=Q864|lt=Pokémon}}'' and ''{{ill|Future Card Buddyfight|en|Future Card Buddyfight|WD=Q15502589|lt=Future Card Buddyfight}}'', the company also partners with local creators such as {{ill|Johnny Lau|en|Johnny Lau|WD=Q16731275|lt=Johnny Lau}} to publish comic series for distribution in Southeast Asia."[https://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/news-and-events/news/singapore-business-news/Industry/education-through-entertainment.html Education through entertainment]" (). [[:en:Singapore Economic Development Board|Singapore Economic Development Board]]. January 15, 2014. Retrieved on June 2, 2015. ==New Manga Awards== Shogakukan has awards for amateur [[:en:Mangaka|manga artists]] who want to become professional. It allows people to either send in their {{ill|Manga|en|Manga|WD=Q8274|lt=Manga}} by mail or bring it in to an {{ill|Editor|en|Editor|WD=Q1607826|lt=Editor}}.{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Genghis Khan controversy== {{weight|date=May 2023}} On February 15, 2018, ''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' ( "''Gekkan Corocoro Comic''"), a children's magazine published by Shogakukan, had in its March issue a cartoon making fun of {{ill|Genghis Khan|en|Genghis Khan|WD=Q720|lt=Genghis Khan}}, founder of the {{ill|Toluid Civil War|en|Toluid Civil War|WD=Q16871984|lt=Mongol Empire}}. The comic showed a mischievous boy doodling juvenile things on pictures of famous people, such as a dog's face on a picture of {{ill|Albert Einstein|en|Albert Einstein|WD=Q937|lt=Albert Einstein}}. Genghis Khan was depicted with a crude rendering of male genitalia on his forehead.{{cite news|title=Mongolians irate over manga showing penis on Genghis Khan|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=28 February 2018|archive-date=August 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802191717/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Coro Coro Comics Apologizes for Manga's Depiction of Genghis Khan|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2018-02-25/coro-coro-comics-apologizes-for-manga-depiction-of-genghis-khan/.128187|access-date=13 June 2020|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Feb 2018}} After some backlash, Shogakukan initially offered an apology addressed to the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo on February 23, but that failed to mollify Mongolian expats in Japan, who regard Genghis Khan as a national hero. On February 26, Mongolians and citizens of {{ill|China Airlines|en|China Airlines|WD=Q51756|lt=China}}'s {{ill|Inner Mongolia|en|Inner Mongolia|WD=Q41079|lt=Inner Mongolia}} {{ill|Autonomous regions of China|en|Autonomous regions of China|WD=Q57362|lt=autonomous region}} resident in Japan sent a formal letter of protest to Shogakukan, while some 90 demonstrators protested in front of company headquarters. Major bookselling chains {{ill|Kinokuniya|en|Kinokuniya|WD=Q11604928|lt=Kinokuniya}}, Miraiya and Kumazawa pulled the publication off shelves after the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo filed an official complaint with the {{ill|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|en|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|WD=Q222241|lt=Ministry of Foreign Affairs}}.{{cite web|title=Genghis Khan-insulting manga pulled from major book stores amid further Mongolian protests|url=https://soranews24.com/2018/03/01/genghis-khan-insulting-manga-pulled-from-major-book-stores-amid-further-mongolian-protests/|website=SoraNews24|date=March 2018|publisher=Socio Corporation|access-date=13 June 2020}} In March 2018, Shogakukan issued another public apology, announced a national recall of the magazine and offered a refund to magazine patrons.{{cite news|title=Publisher Shogakukan withdraws and apologizes for comic that mocks Genghis Khan|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/03/06/national/japanese-publisher-withdraws-kids-comic-illustration-mocks-mongolian-hero-genghis-khan/|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=Kyodo|publisher=The Japan Times|date=6 March 2018}} CoroCoro Comic's website also published an apology by Asumi Yoshino, author of the serialized manga ''Yarisugi!!! Itazura-kun'' which contained the controversial image.{{cite news|last1=Shiohara|first1=Ken|title=Publisher recalls manga magazine that infuriated Mongolians|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=7 March 2018|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630024803/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|url-status=dead}} ==List of magazines published== ===Manga magazines=== ====Male oriented manga magazines==== ;Children's manga magazines *''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' (since 1977) *''Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic'' (since 1981) *''CoroCoro Ichiban!'' {{ill|Magazine|en|Magazine|WD=Q41298|lt=magazines}}, {{ill|Light novel|en|Light novel|WD=Q747381|lt=light novels}}, [[:en:Japanese dictionaries|dictionaries]], {{ill|Literature|en|Literature|WD=Q8242|lt=Literature}}, {{ill|non-fiction|en|non-fiction|WD=Q213051|lt=non-fiction}}, {{ill|home media|en|home media|WD=Q59149963|lt=home media}}, and other media in Japan.{{cite web|title=Company Overview of SHOGAKUKAN|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapid=5478256|website=Bloomberg|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|access-date=23 April 2018}} Shogakukan founded {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, which also founded {{ill|Hakusensha|en|Hakusensha|WD=Q1155260|lt=Hakusensha}}. These are three separate companies, but are together called the {{ill|Hitotsubashi Group|en|Hitotsubashi Group|WD=Q97352307|lt=Hitotsubashi Group}},{{cite news|title=Global Publishing Leaders 2015: Shogakukan|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/67308-global-publishing-leaders-2015-shogakukan.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=26 Jun 2015}} one of the largest publishing groups in Japan and the world. Shogakukan is headquartered in the Shogakukan Building in {{ill|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|en|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|WD=Q3347238|lt=Hitotsubashi}}, part of {{ill|Kanda, Tokyo|en|Kanda, Tokyo|WD=Q338861|lt=Kanda}}, {{ill|Chiyoda, Tokyo|en|Chiyoda, Tokyo|WD=Q214051|lt=Chiyoda, Tokyo}}, near the [[:en:Jimbocho|Jimbocho]] book district. The corporation also has the other two companies located in the same [[:en:23 special wards|ward]]. ==International operations== ===In the United States=== Shogakukan, along with {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, owns {{ill|Viz Media|en|Viz Media|WD=Q660288|lt=Viz Media}},{{cite news|last1=Alverson|first1=Brigid|title=Hachette and Kadokawa Partner on Manga and Graphic Novels|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/70380-hachette-and-kadokawa-partner-on-manga-and-graphic-novels.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=13 May 2016}} which publishes manga from both companies in the {{ill|United States|en|United States|WD=Q30|lt=United States}}. Shogakukan's licensing arm in North America was '''ShoPro Entertainment'''; it was merged into Viz Media in 2005.{{cite news|title=ShoPro Entertainment Inc. and VIZ, LLC to Merge|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2005-01-25/shopro-entertainment-inc-and-viz-llc-to-merge|access-date=23 April 2018|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Jan 2005}} Shogakukan's production arm is {{ill|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|en|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|WD=Q5356388|lt=Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions}} (previously Shogakukan Productions Co., Ltd.) In March 2010 it was announced that Shogakukan would partner with the American comics publisher {{ill|Fantagraphics|en|Fantagraphics|WD=Q1395850|lt=Fantagraphics}} to issue a line of manga to be edited by {{ill|Rachel Thorn|en|Rachel Thorn|WD=Q15500705|lt=Rachel Thorn}}.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100738/http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|archive-date=September 7, 2015|url=http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|title=Journalista reputation-destroying extra: Four years' work|last=Deppey|first=Dirk|date=March 8, 2010|work=Journalista!|publisher=The Comics Journal|access-date=2015-11-16}} ===In Europe=== In {{ill|Europe|en|Europe|WD=Q46|lt=Europe}}, manga from Shōgakukan and [[:en:Shūeisha|Shūeisha]] are published by local publishers such as {{ill|Pika Édition|en|Pika Édition|WD=Q3388349|lt=Pika Édition}}, {{ill|Ki-oon|en|Ki-oon|WD=Q3196283|lt=Ki-oon}}, {{ill|Kana (publisher)|en|Kana (publisher)|WD=Q2339813|lt=Kana}} and {{ill|Kazé|en|Kazé|WD=Q1582074|lt=Kazé}} for the French market, and Kazé, {{ill|Carlsen Verlag|en|Carlsen Verlag|WD=Q289299|lt=Carlsen}}, [[Egmont Group#Egmont Publishing|Egmont]] and {{ill|Tokyopop|en|Tokyopop|WD=Q315736|lt=Tokyopop}} for the German market. Shogakukan, Shueisha and ShoPro have established a joint venture named [[:en:Viz Media Europe|Viz Media Europe]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |title=Vizmedia Europe rachète le groupe Kazé |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181304/http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |url-status=dead }} Viz Media Europe bought in 2009 the French Kazé Group whose activities are mainly publishing manga and home video for the French and German market.{{Cite web |url=http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |title=Organisation du groupe Vizmedia Europe |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627071327/http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |url-status=dead }} ===In Southeast Asia=== The company has a wholly-owned subsidiary, {{ill|Shogakukan Asia|en|Shogakukan Asia|WD=Q20539280|lt=Shogakukan Asia}}, with headquarter in {{ill|Singapore|en|Singapore|WD=Q334|lt=Singapore}}. Besides producing popular titles in English such as ''{{ill|Case Closed|en|Case Closed|WD=Q3853685|lt=Detective Conan}}'', ''{{ill|Pokémon|en|Pokémon|WD=Q864|lt=Pokémon}}'' and ''{{ill|Future Card Buddyfight|en|Future Card Buddyfight|WD=Q15502589|lt=Future Card Buddyfight}}'', the company also partners with local creators such as {{ill|Johnny Lau|en|Johnny Lau|WD=Q16731275|lt=Johnny Lau}} to publish comic series for distribution in Southeast Asia."[https://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/news-and-events/news/singapore-business-news/Industry/education-through-entertainment.html Education through entertainment]" (). [[:en:Singapore Economic Development Board|Singapore Economic Development Board]]. January 15, 2014. Retrieved on June 2, 2015. ==New Manga Awards== Shogakukan has awards for amateur [[:en:Mangaka|manga artists]] who want to become professional. It allows people to either send in their {{ill|Manga|en|Manga|WD=Q8274|lt=Manga}} by mail or bring it in to an {{ill|Editor|en|Editor|WD=Q1607826|lt=Editor}}.{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Genghis Khan controversy== {{weight|date=May 2023}} On February 15, 2018, ''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' ( "''Gekkan Corocoro Comic''"), a children's magazine published by Shogakukan, had in its March issue a cartoon making fun of {{ill|Genghis Khan|en|Genghis Khan|WD=Q720|lt=Genghis Khan}}, founder of the {{ill|Toluid Civil War|en|Toluid Civil War|WD=Q16871984|lt=Mongol Empire}}. The comic showed a mischievous boy doodling juvenile things on pictures of famous people, such as a dog's face on a picture of {{ill|Albert Einstein|en|Albert Einstein|WD=Q937|lt=Albert Einstein}}. Genghis Khan was depicted with a crude rendering of male genitalia on his forehead.{{cite news|title=Mongolians irate over manga showing penis on Genghis Khan|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=28 February 2018|archive-date=August 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802191717/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Coro Coro Comics Apologizes for Manga's Depiction of Genghis Khan|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2018-02-25/coro-coro-comics-apologizes-for-manga-depiction-of-genghis-khan/.128187|access-date=13 June 2020|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Feb 2018}} After some backlash, Shogakukan initially offered an apology addressed to the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo on February 23, but that failed to mollify Mongolian expats in Japan, who regard Genghis Khan as a national hero. On February 26, Mongolians and citizens of {{ill|China Airlines|en|China Airlines|WD=Q51756|lt=China}}'s {{ill|Inner Mongolia|en|Inner Mongolia|WD=Q41079|lt=Inner Mongolia}} {{ill|Autonomous regions of China|en|Autonomous regions of China|WD=Q57362|lt=autonomous region}} resident in Japan sent a formal letter of protest to Shogakukan, while some 90 demonstrators protested in front of company headquarters. Major bookselling chains {{ill|Kinokuniya|en|Kinokuniya|WD=Q11604928|lt=Kinokuniya}}, Miraiya and Kumazawa pulled the publication off shelves after the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo filed an official complaint with the {{ill|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|en|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|WD=Q222241|lt=Ministry of Foreign Affairs}}.{{cite web|title=Genghis Khan-insulting manga pulled from major book stores amid further Mongolian protests|url=https://soranews24.com/2018/03/01/genghis-khan-insulting-manga-pulled-from-major-book-stores-amid-further-mongolian-protests/|website=SoraNews24|date=March 2018|publisher=Socio Corporation|access-date=13 June 2020}} In March 2018, Shogakukan issued another public apology, announced a national recall of the magazine and offered a refund to magazine patrons.{{cite news|title=Publisher Shogakukan withdraws and apologizes for comic that mocks Genghis Khan|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/03/06/national/japanese-publisher-withdraws-kids-comic-illustration-mocks-mongolian-hero-genghis-khan/|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=Kyodo|publisher=The Japan Times|date=6 March 2018}} CoroCoro Comic's website also published an apology by Asumi Yoshino, author of the serialized manga ''Yarisugi!!! Itazura-kun'' which contained the controversial image.{{cite news|last1=Shiohara|first1=Ken|title=Publisher recalls manga magazine that infuriated Mongolians|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=7 March 2018|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630024803/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|url-status=dead}} ==List of magazines published== ===Manga magazines=== ====Male oriented manga magazines==== ;Children's manga magazines *''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' (since 1977) *''Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic'' (since 1981) *''CoroCoro Ichiban!'' {{ill|Magazine|en|Magazine|WD=Q41298|lt=magazines}}, {{ill|Light novel|en|Light novel|WD=Q747381|lt=light novels}}, [[:en:Japanese dictionaries|dictionaries]], {{ill|Literature|en|Literature|WD=Q8242|lt=Literature}}, {{ill|non-fiction|en|non-fiction|WD=Q213051|lt=non-fiction}}, {{ill|home media|en|home media|WD=Q59149963|lt=home media}}, and other media in Japan.{{cite web|title=Company Overview of SHOGAKUKAN|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapid=5478256|website=Bloomberg|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|access-date=23 April 2018}} Shogakukan founded {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, which also founded {{ill|Hakusensha|en|Hakusensha|WD=Q1155260|lt=Hakusensha}}. These are three separate companies, but are together called the {{ill|Hitotsubashi Group|en|Hitotsubashi Group|WD=Q97352307|lt=Hitotsubashi Group}},{{cite news|title=Global Publishing Leaders 2015: Shogakukan|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/67308-global-publishing-leaders-2015-shogakukan.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=26 Jun 2015}} one of the largest publishing groups in Japan and the world. Shogakukan is headquartered in the Shogakukan Building in {{ill|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|en|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|WD=Q3347238|lt=Hitotsubashi}}, part of {{ill|Kanda, Tokyo|en|Kanda, Tokyo|WD=Q338861|lt=Kanda}}, {{ill|Chiyoda, Tokyo|en|Chiyoda, Tokyo|WD=Q214051|lt=Chiyoda, Tokyo}}, near the [[:en:Jimbocho|Jimbocho]] book district. The corporation also has the other two companies located in the same [[:en:23 special wards|ward]]. ==International operations== ===In the United States=== Shogakukan, along with {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, owns {{ill|Viz Media|en|Viz Media|WD=Q660288|lt=Viz Media}},{{cite news|last1=Alverson|first1=Brigid|title=Hachette and Kadokawa Partner on Manga and Graphic Novels|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/70380-hachette-and-kadokawa-partner-on-manga-and-graphic-novels.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=13 May 2016}} which publishes manga from both companies in the {{ill|United States|en|United States|WD=Q30|lt=United States}}. Shogakukan's licensing arm in North America was '''ShoPro Entertainment'''; it was merged into Viz Media in 2005.{{cite news|title=ShoPro Entertainment Inc. and VIZ, LLC to Merge|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2005-01-25/shopro-entertainment-inc-and-viz-llc-to-merge|access-date=23 April 2018|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Jan 2005}} Shogakukan's production arm is {{ill|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|en|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|WD=Q5356388|lt=Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions}} (previously Shogakukan Productions Co., Ltd.) In March 2010 it was announced that Shogakukan would partner with the American comics publisher {{ill|Fantagraphics|en|Fantagraphics|WD=Q1395850|lt=Fantagraphics}} to issue a line of manga to be edited by {{ill|Rachel Thorn|en|Rachel Thorn|WD=Q15500705|lt=Rachel Thorn}}.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100738/http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|archive-date=September 7, 2015|url=http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|title=Journalista reputation-destroying extra: Four years' work|last=Deppey|first=Dirk|date=March 8, 2010|work=Journalista!|publisher=The Comics Journal|access-date=2015-11-16}} ===In Europe=== In {{ill|Europe|en|Europe|WD=Q46|lt=Europe}}, manga from Shōgakukan and [[:en:Shūeisha|Shūeisha]] are published by local publishers such as {{ill|Pika Édition|en|Pika Édition|WD=Q3388349|lt=Pika Édition}}, {{ill|Ki-oon|en|Ki-oon|WD=Q3196283|lt=Ki-oon}}, {{ill|Kana (publisher)|en|Kana (publisher)|WD=Q2339813|lt=Kana}} and {{ill|Kazé|en|Kazé|WD=Q1582074|lt=Kazé}} for the French market, and Kazé, {{ill|Carlsen Verlag|en|Carlsen Verlag|WD=Q289299|lt=Carlsen}}, [[Egmont Group#Egmont Publishing|Egmont]] and {{ill|Tokyopop|en|Tokyopop|WD=Q315736|lt=Tokyopop}} for the German market. Shogakukan, Shueisha and ShoPro have established a joint venture named [[:en:Viz Media Europe|Viz Media Europe]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |title=Vizmedia Europe rachète le groupe Kazé |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181304/http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |url-status=dead }} Viz Media Europe bought in 2009 the French Kazé Group whose activities are mainly publishing manga and home video for the French and German market.{{Cite web |url=http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |title=Organisation du groupe Vizmedia Europe |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627071327/http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |url-status=dead }} ===In Southeast Asia=== The company has a wholly-owned subsidiary, {{ill|Shogakukan Asia|en|Shogakukan Asia|WD=Q20539280|lt=Shogakukan Asia}}, with headquarter in {{ill|Singapore|en|Singapore|WD=Q334|lt=Singapore}}. Besides producing popular titles in English such as ''{{ill|Case Closed|en|Case Closed|WD=Q3853685|lt=Detective Conan}}'', ''{{ill|Pokémon|en|Pokémon|WD=Q864|lt=Pokémon}}'' and ''{{ill|Future Card Buddyfight|en|Future Card Buddyfight|WD=Q15502589|lt=Future Card Buddyfight}}'', the company also partners with local creators such as {{ill|Johnny Lau|en|Johnny Lau|WD=Q16731275|lt=Johnny Lau}} to publish comic series for distribution in Southeast Asia."[https://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/news-and-events/news/singapore-business-news/Industry/education-through-entertainment.html Education through entertainment]" (). [[:en:Singapore Economic Development Board|Singapore Economic Development Board]]. January 15, 2014. Retrieved on June 2, 2015. ==New Manga Awards== Shogakukan has awards for amateur [[:en:Mangaka|manga artists]] who want to become professional. It allows people to either send in their {{ill|Manga|en|Manga|WD=Q8274|lt=Manga}} by mail or bring it in to an {{ill|Editor|en|Editor|WD=Q1607826|lt=Editor}}.{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Genghis Khan controversy== {{weight|date=May 2023}} On February 15, 2018, ''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' ( "''Gekkan Corocoro Comic''"), a children's magazine published by Shogakukan, had in its March issue a cartoon making fun of {{ill|Genghis Khan|en|Genghis Khan|WD=Q720|lt=Genghis Khan}}, founder of the {{ill|Toluid Civil War|en|Toluid Civil War|WD=Q16871984|lt=Mongol Empire}}. The comic showed a mischievous boy doodling juvenile things on pictures of famous people, such as a dog's face on a picture of {{ill|Albert Einstein|en|Albert Einstein|WD=Q937|lt=Albert Einstein}}. Genghis Khan was depicted with a crude rendering of male genitalia on his forehead.{{cite news|title=Mongolians irate over manga showing penis on Genghis Khan|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=28 February 2018|archive-date=August 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802191717/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Coro Coro Comics Apologizes for Manga's Depiction of Genghis Khan|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2018-02-25/coro-coro-comics-apologizes-for-manga-depiction-of-genghis-khan/.128187|access-date=13 June 2020|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Feb 2018}} After some backlash, Shogakukan initially offered an apology addressed to the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo on February 23, but that failed to mollify Mongolian expats in Japan, who regard Genghis Khan as a national hero. On February 26, Mongolians and citizens of {{ill|China Airlines|en|China Airlines|WD=Q51756|lt=China}}'s {{ill|Inner Mongolia|en|Inner Mongolia|WD=Q41079|lt=Inner Mongolia}} {{ill|Autonomous regions of China|en|Autonomous regions of China|WD=Q57362|lt=autonomous region}} resident in Japan sent a formal letter of protest to Shogakukan, while some 90 demonstrators protested in front of company headquarters. Major bookselling chains {{ill|Kinokuniya|en|Kinokuniya|WD=Q11604928|lt=Kinokuniya}}, Miraiya and Kumazawa pulled the publication off shelves after the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo filed an official complaint with the {{ill|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|en|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|WD=Q222241|lt=Ministry of Foreign Affairs}}.{{cite web|title=Genghis Khan-insulting manga pulled from major book stores amid further Mongolian protests|url=https://soranews24.com/2018/03/01/genghis-khan-insulting-manga-pulled-from-major-book-stores-amid-further-mongolian-protests/|website=SoraNews24|date=March 2018|publisher=Socio Corporation|access-date=13 June 2020}} In March 2018, Shogakukan issued another public apology, announced a national recall of the magazine and offered a refund to magazine patrons.{{cite news|title=Publisher Shogakukan withdraws and apologizes for comic that mocks Genghis Khan|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/03/06/national/japanese-publisher-withdraws-kids-comic-illustration-mocks-mongolian-hero-genghis-khan/|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=Kyodo|publisher=The Japan Times|date=6 March 2018}} CoroCoro Comic's website also published an apology by Asumi Yoshino, author of the serialized manga ''Yarisugi!!! Itazura-kun'' which contained the controversial image.{{cite news|last1=Shiohara|first1=Ken|title=Publisher recalls manga magazine that infuriated Mongolians|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=7 March 2018|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630024803/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|url-status=dead}} ==List of magazines published== ===Manga magazines=== ====Male oriented manga magazines==== ;Children's manga magazines *''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' (since 1977) *''Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic'' (since 1981) *''CoroCoro Ichiban!'' April 2018}} Shogakukan founded {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, which also founded {{ill|Hakusensha|en|Hakusensha|WD=Q1155260|lt=Hakusensha}}. These are three separate companies, but are together called the {{ill|Hitotsubashi Group|en|Hitotsubashi Group|WD=Q97352307|lt=Hitotsubashi Group}},{{cite news|title=Global Publishing Leaders 2015: Shogakukan|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/67308-global-publishing-leaders-2015-shogakukan.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=26 Jun 2015}} one of the largest publishing groups in Japan and the world. Shogakukan is headquartered in the Shogakukan Building in {{ill|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|en|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|WD=Q3347238|lt=Hitotsubashi}}, part of {{ill|Kanda, Tokyo|en|Kanda, Tokyo|WD=Q338861|lt=Kanda}}, {{ill|Chiyoda, Tokyo|en|Chiyoda, Tokyo|WD=Q214051|lt=Chiyoda, Tokyo}}, near the [[:en:Jimbocho|Jimbocho]] book district. The corporation also has the other two companies located in the same [[:en:23 special wards|ward]]. ==International operations== ===In the United States=== Shogakukan, along with {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, owns {{ill|Viz Media|en|Viz Media|WD=Q660288|lt=Viz Media}},{{cite news|last1=Alverson|first1=Brigid|title=Hachette and Kadokawa Partner on Manga and Graphic Novels|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/70380-hachette-and-kadokawa-partner-on-manga-and-graphic-novels.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=13 May 2016}} which publishes manga from both companies in the {{ill|United States|en|United States|WD=Q30|lt=United States}}. Shogakukan's licensing arm in North America was '''ShoPro Entertainment'''; it was merged into Viz Media in 2005.{{cite news|title=ShoPro Entertainment Inc. and VIZ, LLC to Merge|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2005-01-25/shopro-entertainment-inc-and-viz-llc-to-merge|access-date=23 April 2018|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Jan 2005}} Shogakukan's production arm is {{ill|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|en|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|WD=Q5356388|lt=Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions}} (previously Shogakukan Productions Co., Ltd.) In March 2010 it was announced that Shogakukan would partner with the American comics publisher {{ill|Fantagraphics|en|Fantagraphics|WD=Q1395850|lt=Fantagraphics}} to issue a line of manga to be edited by {{ill|Rachel Thorn|en|Rachel Thorn|WD=Q15500705|lt=Rachel Thorn}}.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100738/http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|archive-date=September 7, 2015|url=http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|title=Journalista reputation-destroying extra: Four years' work|last=Deppey|first=Dirk|date=March 8, 2010|work=Journalista!|publisher=The Comics Journal|access-date=2015-11-16}} ===In Europe=== In {{ill|Europe|en|Europe|WD=Q46|lt=Europe}}, manga from Shōgakukan and [[:en:Shūeisha|Shūeisha]] are published by local publishers such as {{ill|Pika Édition|en|Pika Édition|WD=Q3388349|lt=Pika Édition}}, {{ill|Ki-oon|en|Ki-oon|WD=Q3196283|lt=Ki-oon}}, {{ill|Kana (publisher)|en|Kana (publisher)|WD=Q2339813|lt=Kana}} and {{ill|Kazé|en|Kazé|WD=Q1582074|lt=Kazé}} for the French market, and Kazé, {{ill|Carlsen Verlag|en|Carlsen Verlag|WD=Q289299|lt=Carlsen}}, [[Egmont Group#Egmont Publishing|Egmont]] and {{ill|Tokyopop|en|Tokyopop|WD=Q315736|lt=Tokyopop}} for the German market. Shogakukan, Shueisha and ShoPro have established a joint venture named [[:en:Viz Media Europe|Viz Media Europe]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |title=Vizmedia Europe rachète le groupe Kazé |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181304/http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |url-status=dead }} Viz Media Europe bought in 2009 the French Kazé Group whose activities are mainly publishing manga and home video for the French and German market.{{Cite web |url=http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |title=Organisation du groupe Vizmedia Europe |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627071327/http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |url-status=dead }} ===In Southeast Asia=== The company has a wholly-owned subsidiary, {{ill|Shogakukan Asia|en|Shogakukan Asia|WD=Q20539280|lt=Shogakukan Asia}}, with headquarter in {{ill|Singapore|en|Singapore|WD=Q334|lt=Singapore}}. Besides producing popular titles in English such as ''{{ill|Case Closed|en|Case Closed|WD=Q3853685|lt=Detective Conan}}'', ''{{ill|Pokémon|en|Pokémon|WD=Q864|lt=Pokémon}}'' and ''{{ill|Future Card Buddyfight|en|Future Card Buddyfight|WD=Q15502589|lt=Future Card Buddyfight}}'', the company also partners with local creators such as {{ill|Johnny Lau|en|Johnny Lau|WD=Q16731275|lt=Johnny Lau}} to publish comic series for distribution in Southeast Asia."[https://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/news-and-events/news/singapore-business-news/Industry/education-through-entertainment.html Education through entertainment]" (). [[:en:Singapore Economic Development Board|Singapore Economic Development Board]]. January 15, 2014. Retrieved on June 2, 2015. ==New Manga Awards== Shogakukan has awards for amateur [[:en:Mangaka|manga artists]] who want to become professional. It allows people to either send in their {{ill|Manga|en|Manga|WD=Q8274|lt=Manga}} by mail or bring it in to an {{ill|Editor|en|Editor|WD=Q1607826|lt=Editor}}.{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Genghis Khan controversy== {{weight|date=May 2023}} On February 15, 2018, ''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' ( "''Gekkan Corocoro Comic''"), a children's magazine published by Shogakukan, had in its March issue a cartoon making fun of {{ill|Genghis Khan|en|Genghis Khan|WD=Q720|lt=Genghis Khan}}, founder of the {{ill|Toluid Civil War|en|Toluid Civil War|WD=Q16871984|lt=Mongol Empire}}. The comic showed a mischievous boy doodling juvenile things on pictures of famous people, such as a dog's face on a picture of {{ill|Albert Einstein|en|Albert Einstein|WD=Q937|lt=Albert Einstein}}. Genghis Khan was depicted with a crude rendering of male genitalia on his forehead.{{cite news|title=Mongolians irate over manga showing penis on Genghis Khan|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=28 February 2018|archive-date=August 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802191717/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Coro Coro Comics Apologizes for Manga's Depiction of Genghis Khan|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2018-02-25/coro-coro-comics-apologizes-for-manga-depiction-of-genghis-khan/.128187|access-date=13 June 2020|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Feb 2018}} After some backlash, Shogakukan initially offered an apology addressed to the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo on February 23, but that failed to mollify Mongolian expats in Japan, who regard Genghis Khan as a national hero. On February 26, Mongolians and citizens of {{ill|China Airlines|en|China Airlines|WD=Q51756|lt=China}}'s {{ill|Inner Mongolia|en|Inner Mongolia|WD=Q41079|lt=Inner Mongolia}} {{ill|Autonomous regions of China|en|Autonomous regions of China|WD=Q57362|lt=autonomous region}} resident in Japan sent a formal letter of protest to Shogakukan, while some 90 demonstrators protested in front of company headquarters. Major bookselling chains {{ill|Kinokuniya|en|Kinokuniya|WD=Q11604928|lt=Kinokuniya}}, Miraiya and Kumazawa pulled the publication off shelves after the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo filed an official complaint with the {{ill|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|en|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|WD=Q222241|lt=Ministry of Foreign Affairs}}.{{cite web|title=Genghis Khan-insulting manga pulled from major book stores amid further Mongolian protests|url=https://soranews24.com/2018/03/01/genghis-khan-insulting-manga-pulled-from-major-book-stores-amid-further-mongolian-protests/|website=SoraNews24|date=March 2018|publisher=Socio Corporation|access-date=13 June 2020}} In March 2018, Shogakukan issued another public apology, announced a national recall of the magazine and offered a refund to magazine patrons.{{cite news|title=Publisher Shogakukan withdraws and apologizes for comic that mocks Genghis Khan|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/03/06/national/japanese-publisher-withdraws-kids-comic-illustration-mocks-mongolian-hero-genghis-khan/|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=Kyodo|publisher=The Japan Times|date=6 March 2018}} CoroCoro Comic's website also published an apology by Asumi Yoshino, author of the serialized manga ''Yarisugi!!! Itazura-kun'' which contained the controversial image.{{cite news|last1=Shiohara|first1=Ken|title=Publisher recalls manga magazine that infuriated Mongolians|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=7 March 2018|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630024803/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|url-status=dead}} ==List of magazines published== ===Manga magazines=== ====Male oriented manga magazines==== ;Children's manga magazines *''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' (since 1977) *''Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic'' (since 1981) *''CoroCoro Ichiban!'' April 2018}} Shogakukan founded {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, which also founded {{ill|Hakusensha|en|Hakusensha|WD=Q1155260|lt=Hakusensha}}. These are three separate companies, but are together called the {{ill|Hitotsubashi Group|en|Hitotsubashi Group|WD=Q97352307|lt=Hitotsubashi Group}},{{cite news|title=Global Publishing Leaders 2015: Shogakukan|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/67308-global-publishing-leaders-2015-shogakukan.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=26 Jun 2015}} one of the largest publishing groups in Japan and the world. Shogakukan is headquartered in the Shogakukan Building in {{ill|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|en|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|WD=Q3347238|lt=Hitotsubashi}}, part of {{ill|Kanda, Tokyo|en|Kanda, Tokyo|WD=Q338861|lt=Kanda}}, {{ill|Chiyoda, Tokyo|en|Chiyoda, Tokyo|WD=Q214051|lt=Chiyoda, Tokyo}}, near the [[:en:Jimbocho|Jimbocho]] book district. The corporation also has the other two companies located in the same [[:en:23 special wards|ward]]. ==International operations== ===In the United States=== Shogakukan, along with {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, owns {{ill|Viz Media|en|Viz Media|WD=Q660288|lt=Viz Media}},{{cite news|last1=Alverson|first1=Brigid|title=Hachette and Kadokawa Partner on Manga and Graphic Novels|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/70380-hachette-and-kadokawa-partner-on-manga-and-graphic-novels.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=13 May 2016}} which publishes manga from both companies in the {{ill|United States|en|United States|WD=Q30|lt=United States}}. Shogakukan's licensing arm in North America was '''ShoPro Entertainment'''; it was merged into Viz Media in 2005.{{cite news|title=ShoPro Entertainment Inc. and VIZ, LLC to Merge|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2005-01-25/shopro-entertainment-inc-and-viz-llc-to-merge|access-date=23 April 2018|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Jan 2005}} Shogakukan's production arm is {{ill|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|en|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|WD=Q5356388|lt=Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions}} (previously Shogakukan Productions Co., Ltd.) In March 2010 it was announced that Shogakukan would partner with the American comics publisher {{ill|Fantagraphics|en|Fantagraphics|WD=Q1395850|lt=Fantagraphics}} to issue a line of manga to be edited by {{ill|Rachel Thorn|en|Rachel Thorn|WD=Q15500705|lt=Rachel Thorn}}.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100738/http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|archive-date=September 7, 2015|url=http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|title=Journalista reputation-destroying extra: Four years' work|last=Deppey|first=Dirk|date=March 8, 2010|work=Journalista!|publisher=The Comics Journal|access-date=2015-11-16}} ===In Europe=== In {{ill|Europe|en|Europe|WD=Q46|lt=Europe}}, manga from Shōgakukan and [[:en:Shūeisha|Shūeisha]] are published by local publishers such as {{ill|Pika Édition|en|Pika Édition|WD=Q3388349|lt=Pika Édition}}, {{ill|Ki-oon|en|Ki-oon|WD=Q3196283|lt=Ki-oon}}, {{ill|Kana (publisher)|en|Kana (publisher)|WD=Q2339813|lt=Kana}} and {{ill|Kazé|en|Kazé|WD=Q1582074|lt=Kazé}} for the French market, and Kazé, {{ill|Carlsen Verlag|en|Carlsen Verlag|WD=Q289299|lt=Carlsen}}, [[Egmont Group#Egmont Publishing|Egmont]] and {{ill|Tokyopop|en|Tokyopop|WD=Q315736|lt=Tokyopop}} for the German market. Shogakukan, Shueisha and ShoPro have established a joint venture named [[:en:Viz Media Europe|Viz Media Europe]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |title=Vizmedia Europe rachète le groupe Kazé |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181304/http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |url-status=dead }} Viz Media Europe bought in 2009 the French Kazé Group whose activities are mainly publishing manga and home video for the French and German market.{{Cite web |url=http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |title=Organisation du groupe Vizmedia Europe |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627071327/http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |url-status=dead }} ===In Southeast Asia=== The company has a wholly-owned subsidiary, {{ill|Shogakukan Asia|en|Shogakukan Asia|WD=Q20539280|lt=Shogakukan Asia}}, with headquarter in {{ill|Singapore|en|Singapore|WD=Q334|lt=Singapore}}. Besides producing popular titles in English such as ''{{ill|Case Closed|en|Case Closed|WD=Q3853685|lt=Detective Conan}}'', ''{{ill|Pokémon|en|Pokémon|WD=Q864|lt=Pokémon}}'' and ''{{ill|Future Card Buddyfight|en|Future Card Buddyfight|WD=Q15502589|lt=Future Card Buddyfight}}'', the company also partners with local creators such as {{ill|Johnny Lau|en|Johnny Lau|WD=Q16731275|lt=Johnny Lau}} to publish comic series for distribution in Southeast Asia."[https://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/news-and-events/news/singapore-business-news/Industry/education-through-entertainment.html Education through entertainment]" (). [[:en:Singapore Economic Development Board|Singapore Economic Development Board]]. January 15, 2014. Retrieved on June 2, 2015. ==New Manga Awards== Shogakukan has awards for amateur [[:en:Mangaka|manga artists]] who want to become professional. It allows people to either send in their {{ill|Manga|en|Manga|WD=Q8274|lt=Manga}} by mail or bring it in to an {{ill|Editor|en|Editor|WD=Q1607826|lt=Editor}}.{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Genghis Khan controversy== {{weight|date=May 2023}} On February 15, 2018, ''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' ( "''Gekkan Corocoro Comic''"), a children's magazine published by Shogakukan, had in its March issue a cartoon making fun of {{ill|Genghis Khan|en|Genghis Khan|WD=Q720|lt=Genghis Khan}}, founder of the {{ill|Toluid Civil War|en|Toluid Civil War|WD=Q16871984|lt=Mongol Empire}}. The comic showed a mischievous boy doodling juvenile things on pictures of famous people, such as a dog's face on a picture of {{ill|Albert Einstein|en|Albert Einstein|WD=Q937|lt=Albert Einstein}}. Genghis Khan was depicted with a crude rendering of male genitalia on his forehead.{{cite news|title=Mongolians irate over manga showing penis on Genghis Khan|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=28 February 2018|archive-date=August 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802191717/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Coro Coro Comics Apologizes for Manga's Depiction of Genghis Khan|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2018-02-25/coro-coro-comics-apologizes-for-manga-depiction-of-genghis-khan/.128187|access-date=13 June 2020|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Feb 2018}} After some backlash, Shogakukan initially offered an apology addressed to the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo on February 23, but that failed to mollify Mongolian expats in Japan, who regard Genghis Khan as a national hero. On February 26, Mongolians and citizens of {{ill|China Airlines|en|China Airlines|WD=Q51756|lt=China}}'s {{ill|Inner Mongolia|en|Inner Mongolia|WD=Q41079|lt=Inner Mongolia}} {{ill|Autonomous regions of China|en|Autonomous regions of China|WD=Q57362|lt=autonomous region}} resident in Japan sent a formal letter of protest to Shogakukan, while some 90 demonstrators protested in front of company headquarters. Major bookselling chains {{ill|Kinokuniya|en|Kinokuniya|WD=Q11604928|lt=Kinokuniya}}, Miraiya and Kumazawa pulled the publication off shelves after the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo filed an official complaint with the {{ill|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|en|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|WD=Q222241|lt=Ministry of Foreign Affairs}}.{{cite web|title=Genghis Khan-insulting manga pulled from major book stores amid further Mongolian protests|url=https://soranews24.com/2018/03/01/genghis-khan-insulting-manga-pulled-from-major-book-stores-amid-further-mongolian-protests/|website=SoraNews24|date=March 2018|publisher=Socio Corporation|access-date=13 June 2020}} In March 2018, Shogakukan issued another public apology, announced a national recall of the magazine and offered a refund to magazine patrons.{{cite news|title=Publisher Shogakukan withdraws and apologizes for comic that mocks Genghis Khan|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/03/06/national/japanese-publisher-withdraws-kids-comic-illustration-mocks-mongolian-hero-genghis-khan/|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=Kyodo|publisher=The Japan Times|date=6 March 2018}} CoroCoro Comic's website also published an apology by Asumi Yoshino, author of the serialized manga ''Yarisugi!!! Itazura-kun'' which contained the controversial image.{{cite news|last1=Shiohara|first1=Ken|title=Publisher recalls manga magazine that infuriated Mongolians|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=7 March 2018|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630024803/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|url-status=dead}} ==List of magazines published== ===Manga magazines=== ====Male oriented manga magazines==== ;Children's manga magazines *''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' (since 1977) *''Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic'' (since 1981) *''CoroCoro Ichiban!'' April 2018}} Shogakukan founded {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, which also founded {{ill|Hakusensha|en|Hakusensha|WD=Q1155260|lt=Hakusensha}}. Shogakukan is headquartered in the Shogakukan Building in {{ill|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|en|Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|WD=Q3347238|lt=Hitotsubashi}}, part of {{ill|Kanda, Tokyo|en|Kanda, Tokyo|WD=Q338861|lt=Kanda}}, {{ill|Chiyoda, Tokyo|en|Chiyoda, Tokyo|WD=Q214051|lt=Chiyoda, Tokyo}}, near the [[:en:Jimbocho|Jimbocho]] book district. The corporation also has the other two companies located in the same [[:en:23 special wards|ward]]. ==International operations== ===In the United States=== Shogakukan, along with {{ill|Shueisha|en|Shueisha|WD=Q844822|lt=Shueisha}}, owns {{ill|Viz Media|en|Viz Media|WD=Q660288|lt=Viz Media}},{{cite news|last1=Alverson|first1=Brigid|title=Hachette and Kadokawa Partner on Manga and Graphic Novels|url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/70380-hachette-and-kadokawa-partner-on-manga-and-graphic-novels.html|access-date=23 April 2018|agency=Publishers Weekly|publisher=PWxyz|date=13 May 2016}} which publishes manga from both companies in the {{ill|United States|en|United States|WD=Q30|lt=United States}}. Shogakukan's licensing arm in North America was '''ShoPro Entertainment'''; it was merged into Viz Media in 2005.{{cite news|title=ShoPro Entertainment Inc. and VIZ, LLC to Merge|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/press-release/2005-01-25/shopro-entertainment-inc-and-viz-llc-to-merge|access-date=23 April 2018|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Jan 2005}} Shogakukan's production arm is {{ill|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|en|Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions|WD=Q5356388|lt=Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions}} (previously Shogakukan Productions Co., Ltd.) In March 2010 it was announced that Shogakukan would partner with the American comics publisher {{ill|Fantagraphics|en|Fantagraphics|WD=Q1395850|lt=Fantagraphics}} to issue a line of manga to be edited by {{ill|Rachel Thorn|en|Rachel Thorn|WD=Q15500705|lt=Rachel Thorn}}.{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907100738/http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|archive-date=September 7, 2015|url=http://classic.tcj.com/manga/journalista-reputation-destroying-extra-four-years-work/|title=Journalista reputation-destroying extra: Four years' work|last=Deppey|first=Dirk|date=March 8, 2010|work=Journalista!|publisher=The Comics Journal|access-date=2015-11-16}} ===In Europe=== In {{ill|Europe|en|Europe|WD=Q46|lt=Europe}}, manga from Shōgakukan and [[:en:Shūeisha|Shūeisha]] are published by local publishers such as {{ill|Pika Édition|en|Pika Édition|WD=Q3388349|lt=Pika Édition}}, {{ill|Ki-oon|en|Ki-oon|WD=Q3196283|lt=Ki-oon}}, {{ill|Kana (publisher)|en|Kana (publisher)|WD=Q2339813|lt=Kana}} and {{ill|Kazé|en|Kazé|WD=Q1582074|lt=Kazé}} for the French market, and Kazé, {{ill|Carlsen Verlag|en|Carlsen Verlag|WD=Q289299|lt=Carlsen}}, [[Egmont Group#Egmont Publishing|Egmont]] and {{ill|Tokyopop|en|Tokyopop|WD=Q315736|lt=Tokyopop}} for the German market. Shogakukan, Shueisha and ShoPro have established a joint venture named [[:en:Viz Media Europe|Viz Media Europe]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |title=Vizmedia Europe rachète le groupe Kazé |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181304/http://www.animeland.com/news/voir/1301/SCOOP-Kaze-rachete |url-status=dead }} Viz Media Europe bought in 2009 the French Kazé Group whose activities are mainly publishing manga and home video for the French and German market.{{Cite web |url=http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |title=Organisation du groupe Vizmedia Europe |access-date=February 18, 2013 |archive-date=June 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627071327/http://vizeurope.com/fr/le-groupe |url-status=dead }} ===In Southeast Asia=== The company has a wholly-owned subsidiary, {{ill|Shogakukan Asia|en|Shogakukan Asia|WD=Q20539280|lt=Shogakukan Asia}}, with headquarter in {{ill|Singapore|en|Singapore|WD=Q334|lt=Singapore}}. Besides producing popular titles in English such as ''{{ill|Case Closed|en|Case Closed|WD=Q3853685|lt=Detective Conan}}'', ''{{ill|Pokémon|en|Pokémon|WD=Q864|lt=Pokémon}}'' and ''{{ill|Future Card Buddyfight|en|Future Card Buddyfight|WD=Q15502589|lt=Future Card Buddyfight}}'', the company also partners with local creators such as {{ill|Johnny Lau|en|Johnny Lau|WD=Q16731275|lt=Johnny Lau}} to publish comic series for distribution in Southeast Asia."[https://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/news-and-events/news/singapore-business-news/Industry/education-through-entertainment.html Education through entertainment]" (). [[:en:Singapore Economic Development Board|Singapore Economic Development Board]]. January 15, 2014. Retrieved on June 2, 2015. ==New Manga Awards== Shogakukan has awards for amateur [[:en:Mangaka|manga artists]] who want to become professional. It allows people to either send in their {{ill|Manga|en|Manga|WD=Q8274|lt=Manga}} by mail or bring it in to an {{ill|Editor|en|Editor|WD=Q1607826|lt=Editor}}.{{Citation needed|date=June 2020}} ==Genghis Khan controversy== {{weight|date=May 2023}} On February 15, 2018, ''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' ( "''Gekkan Corocoro Comic''"), a children's magazine published by Shogakukan, had in its March issue a cartoon making fun of {{ill|Genghis Khan|en|Genghis Khan|WD=Q720|lt=Genghis Khan}}, founder of the {{ill|Toluid Civil War|en|Toluid Civil War|WD=Q16871984|lt=Mongol Empire}}. The comic showed a mischievous boy doodling juvenile things on pictures of famous people, such as a dog's face on a picture of {{ill|Albert Einstein|en|Albert Einstein|WD=Q937|lt=Albert Einstein}}. Genghis Khan was depicted with a crude rendering of male genitalia on his forehead.{{cite news|title=Mongolians irate over manga showing penis on Genghis Khan|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=28 February 2018|archive-date=August 2, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802191717/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201802280039.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Coro Coro Comics Apologizes for Manga's Depiction of Genghis Khan|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2018-02-25/coro-coro-comics-apologizes-for-manga-depiction-of-genghis-khan/.128187|access-date=13 June 2020|publisher=Anime News Network|date=25 Feb 2018}} After some backlash, Shogakukan initially offered an apology addressed to the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo on February 23, but that failed to mollify Mongolian expats in Japan, who regard Genghis Khan as a national hero. On February 26, Mongolians and citizens of {{ill|China Airlines|en|China Airlines|WD=Q51756|lt=China}}'s {{ill|Inner Mongolia|en|Inner Mongolia|WD=Q41079|lt=Inner Mongolia}} {{ill|Autonomous regions of China|en|Autonomous regions of China|WD=Q57362|lt=autonomous region}} resident in Japan sent a formal letter of protest to Shogakukan, while some 90 demonstrators protested in front of company headquarters. Major bookselling chains {{ill|Kinokuniya|en|Kinokuniya|WD=Q11604928|lt=Kinokuniya}}, Miraiya and Kumazawa pulled the publication off shelves after the Mongolian Embassy in Tokyo filed an official complaint with the {{ill|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|en|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Japan)|WD=Q222241|lt=Ministry of Foreign Affairs}}.{{cite web|title=Genghis Khan-insulting manga pulled from major book stores amid further Mongolian protests|url=https://soranews24.com/2018/03/01/genghis-khan-insulting-manga-pulled-from-major-book-stores-amid-further-mongolian-protests/|website=SoraNews24|date=March 2018|publisher=Socio Corporation|access-date=13 June 2020}} In March 2018, Shogakukan issued another public apology, announced a national recall of the magazine and offered a refund to magazine patrons.{{cite news|title=Publisher Shogakukan withdraws and apologizes for comic that mocks Genghis Khan|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/03/06/national/japanese-publisher-withdraws-kids-comic-illustration-mocks-mongolian-hero-genghis-khan/|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=Kyodo|publisher=The Japan Times|date=6 March 2018}} CoroCoro Comic's website also published an apology by Asumi Yoshino, author of the serialized manga ''Yarisugi!!! Itazura-kun'' which contained the controversial image.{{cite news|last1=Shiohara|first1=Ken|title=Publisher recalls manga magazine that infuriated Mongolians|url=http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|access-date=13 June 2020|agency=The Asahi Shimbun|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=7 March 2018|archive-date=June 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630024803/http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/AJ201803070032.html|url-status=dead}} ==List of magazines published== ===Manga magazines=== ====Male oriented manga magazines==== ;Children's manga magazines *''{{ill|CoroCoro Comic|en|CoroCoro Comic|WD=Q715274|lt=CoroCoro Comic}}'' (since 1977) *''Bessatsu CoroCoro Comic'' (since 1981) *''CoroCoro Ichiban!''
